stale_against_replay.declared_by_the_operator: Scored at d051f24, replayed at cf1dc89. FOUR files under sim/ changed between those commits -- see `sim_changed_since_scoring`, which is DERIVED at emit time and is authoritative; this prose accounts for all four and you should check it against that list rather than believe it. (1) sim/phase1.py at 33807a8: reads/prior_state_reads DECLARATIONS only, and topological_order was re-measured across the pair and is byte-identical -- the engine executes that order, so an unchanged order is an unchanged trajectory. (2) sim/detail.py at fe63d80 and 0e936e8: the sub-grid detail synthesis, imported by tools/ only -- nothing under sim/ imports it, so it is in neither the engine's build nor its step path. (3) and (4) sim/assemble.py and sim/nutrients.py at d580647: decision 1017's pulse knob, added as the parameters deposition_scale (default None) and sources_live (default False) and threaded through the engine build. tools/build_fixture.py calls build_phase1_engine() with NO ARGUMENTS, so neither parameter can reach this replay and the engine object is identical across the whole range. A PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS DECLARATION SAID "exactly two files" and was stale: it was written at replay commit 2d4b825 and carried verbatim across four re-emissions while the stamp moved, and the client caught it on their side before vendoring. The derived list beside this prose exists so that cannot recur.
stale_against_replay.what_the_equivalence_proof_below_does_no: the proof compares this verdict's RUN with this fixture's run. Both are state. The verdict's CODE and the replay's code are different here and nothing below compares them.

sim_changed_since_scoring._what: files under sim/ that changed between the commit the verdict was SCORED at and the commit this payload was REPLAYED at, computed at emit time from the two commits above so it cannot disagree with them.
sim_changed_since_scoring._how_to_read_it: empty means the replay ran the code the verdict was scored against. Non-empty is what the operator's declaration must account for -- and that declaration is prose, so check it against this.

not_evaluable_criteria.name: surface-fire regime
not_evaluable_criteria.renders_as: not a fire-model failure and the banner should not read as one: the REGIME is met -- mean annual area-weighted burned fraction 5.8e-03/yr against a 1e-3 floor, a 173-year rotation. What cannot be evaluated is the survival CONTRAST, because layer 1 carries no pre- and post-burn stem and biomass sums over the burned cells to compare

failed_criteria.name: melt-led discharge peak
failed_criteria.renders_as: the hydrograph is melt-led and misses by a margin, not by a season: the outlet peaks in May and 86.7% of years peak after the melt peak and nearer it than the precipitation peak, against a 90% floor

failed_criteria.name: two-way equilibrium (stationarity)
failed_criteria.renders_as: the basin has not settled: area-weighted cover falls 0.96 to 0.53 across the run and is still moving at the end. On screen that is emptiness -- about a third of the basin carries no individuable vegetation in these windows, so a field drawn per-plant has nowhere to put one

failed_criteria.name: no quantity runs to a bound
failed_criteria.renders_as: the one absorbed quantity a viewer can select is band.pft_fractions, at occupancy 0.79: the composition sits at its lower bound and does not leave. Three more are absorbed and are NOT carried in this fixture, so they cannot be drawn -- band.local_runoff (0.9994), band.pft.biomass_pre_offtake (0.90), band.pft.stem_mortality_flux (0.99)

carried_set.derived_by: emit_schema.carried() -- the contract's own function, imported rather than re-derived (894, §23.815)

taxonomic_rung.keeps_parked: decision 886 -- server-side taxonomic aggregation is parked because the fixture already aggregates. A reader who does not know it is parked will eventually ask for per-taxon values; they are not here and that is the ruling.

node_order._what: HUC10 ids in the engine's NODE-AXIS order. Every node-lattice row is indexed by position in this list.
node_order._why_explicit: a client could infer it from the first appearance of each id in cell_keys, and that inference happens to be right today. It rests on cells being grouped by node ordinal, which nothing promises -- and a wrong node index draws the wrong river's flow, which looks entirely plausible.

cell_areas_m2._what: per-cell area in square metres, cell-indexed exactly as every band-lattice row in this fixture is. The weight for any area-weighted basin mean.
cell_areas_m2._why_it_is_here: the client could not reproduce layer 1's `cover_area_weighted` from the vendored bytes, because the basis is `band_areas.json` and that is not vendored. Asked for and supplied, rather than left to be approximated from a 1 km raster at 5-15% per-cell error -- which would agree with a 0.001-quoted figure closely enough to look like confirmation.
cell_areas_m2._weights_are_real_means: True when `band_areas.json` supplied them from the DEM; False when they are the equal-split placeholder. A run weighted by the placeholder is a DIFFERENT ARTEFACT from one weighted by the DEM, so this is a fact about the numbers and not a note about the tool.
cell_areas_m2.worked_example: area-weighted mean of (1 - band.bare_fraction) over `largest_fire` day 22 reproduces layer 1's `cover_area_weighted` for that water year to ~0.001 (0.6110 against 0.6103; `deepest_winter` 0.5518 against 0.5513). Stated so the block carries a CHECK and not just an array.

cell_keys._what: cell index -> [huc10_id, band]. Every band-lattice array in this fixture is indexed by cell, and the residence layer answers in (node, band) -- this is the join between them, without which the two artefacts cannot be used together at all.
cell_keys._why_it_may_cross: a lattice reaches a client as KEYS (decisions 890, 891). This is the key structure, not a palette: it enumerates which (node, band) pairs exist, which is what residence resolves TO.

largest_fire.name: largest_fire
largest_fire.chosen_by: max burned_fraction_sum over water years >= 751 (the flattest quarter)
largest_fire.trend_caveat: burned_fraction_sum declines across the run, r = -0.981. A maximum over the whole post-spin-up range lands on the cutoff year rather than on a fire, so the window is chosen inside the stationary tail.
largest_fire.note: starts 1 June: the fire season, not the water year

density._what: how much of this window carries vegetation. `choose_windows` selects on fire and on snow and considers vegetation NOWHERE, so this is disclosed rather than implied by the window's name.
density._vegetated_is: sum(band.pft_fractions) > 0. That row is a COMPOSITION -- 1 where anything grows, 0 where nothing does -- so a non-zero sum is exactly 'something grows here'.
density._not_wholly_bare_is: counted on the float32 values as SHIPPED, so it reproduces from the payload
density._quantisation_note: the two differ because cells just below 1.0 round to exactly 1.0 in float32. The difference is the population sitting AT the bare bound, which criterion 8 is about.
density._both_reported_because: `bare < 1` is a STRICTER count than a non-zero composition and the two disagree. Neither is handed over as the answer.
density._biomass_note: reported and NOT conjoined with the cover tests. It is non-zero in nearly every cell, so 'cover AND biomass' equals 'cover' and would publish a stricter-looking number that filters nothing.

deepest_winter.caveat: peak SWE over the eligible years of this run runs 27.5-78.7 mm against §5.5.5's 229-330 mm April-1 reference; this window is its maximum, so it is the deepest winter the run HAS. Whether that clears criterion 1's declared floor is the acceptance verdict's to say and is not restated here.
deepest_winter.note: starts 1 January (calendar day-of-year, as `first_tick` records) and runs 90 days to 31 March -- one day short of the April-1 date §5.5.5's reference is quoted on

client_form.is_a_display_encoding: NOT the fixture. Band rows are quantised to 65,534 levels over each row's REALISED range in its own window -- not over the contract's declared bounds, which are a validity range and gave two rows 3 and 12 usable codes when they were used as a dynamic one (§23.837). Every row carries its own `lo`/`hi` beside `contract_lo`/`contract_hi` so both are readable. 2 row-window(s) here are float64 because they reach below float32's floor; the full precision is in fixture_v1.bin.
client_form.band_rows_quantised_node_rows_not: Band rows are quantised because a colour ramp needs no more. Node rows are carried at full float64 because they are 1,154 wide rather than 5,684, so exactness costs little, and because quantising streamflow over its contract bounds would zero everything below 1.5 m3/s. HOW to render a quantity spanning that range is an open display question; this artefact does not answer it.

largest_fire/node.streamflow.not_quantised_because: the contract's bounds are [0, 100000]; 65,534 levels over that puts everything below 1.52593 at zero, and this row's smallest non-zero value is 5.778e-93

deepest_winter/node.streamflow.not_quantised_because: the contract's bounds are [0, 100000]; 65,534 levels over that puts everything below 1.52593 at zero, and this row's smallest non-zero value is 1.508e-35
